Earnings are behind it and growth is accelerating, so I keep it as the core. Second, CME's market cap and P/E in the book look broken, so I trim it to 3%. Third, JPM's +27.7% is June data, so it goes to 6%. TMUS's negative beta is a one-year artifact. I hold it at 6% for an 11.2% FCF yield confirmed by a raised outlook, not as a hedge. I hold no CVX. Hot October CPI is the real threat to IEF, so I size it at 6% and raise cash to 32%. Our order fills after tonight's AMD and ANET prints, and the NVDA $200 rule still applies.
scout.regime: Late-cycle hawkish-Fed rotation: AI and semis de-gross while defensives and energy lead, into a dense calendar (election, payrolls 6 Nov, CPI ~10-13 Nov, NVDA ~17 Nov, FOMC 9 Dec).

picks.thesis: FY27 Q1 revenue +18.8% and accelerating, Azure demand above supply, 26.9x P/E, flat over 12 months. No earnings binary before late January. Trimmed from 8% for de-grossing concentration.
picks.key_risk: Post-midterm AI de-grossing pushes it below its 50-day and toward the prior drawdown lows

picks.thesis: Q3 beat and raised cash outlook are confirmed facts. 11.2% FCF yield and 14.7x P/E. Held for cash yield and post-earnings drift, not as a structural hedge.
picks.key_risk: 10-year breaks 5.2% and bond proxies de-rate; satellite price war

picks.thesis: 13.8x P/E, 16% volatility, positive curve, no event until January. Trimmed because the growth figure is stale June data and sector internals (BAC, SCHW) are weak.
picks.key_risk: HY spreads widen past 4pp with consumer credit deterioration

picks.thesis: Payrolls 6 Nov: consensus ~50k after 29k and downward revisions, against ~54bp of hikes priced. A weak print rallies the belly. 6% volatility, ~4% carry.
picks.key_risk: Hot October CPI pushes the 10-year above 5.1%

picks.thesis: Sole energy vehicle (no CVX overlap), hedging the Iran/Hormuz tail with WTI near $96. RSI cooled to 48. Sidesteps the COP and OXY earnings binaries.
picks.key_risk: US-Iran deal drops crude 15%+

picks.thesis: Earnings out. 19.9x P/E, 6.3% FCF yield, near its 200-day. Holiday data and AWS capacity commentary are upcoming catalysts.
picks.key_risk: Holiday retail weakness with sentiment at 48; capex exceeding cash flow

picks.thesis: RSI 15, 14.7x P/E on +24.7% growth. No earnings event ahead, and completing the euro bond sale removes a supply overhang.
picks.key_risk: Search decay shows in the numbers; new lows

picks.thesis: Raised 2026 guidance. UBS ($640) and RBC ($600) lifted targets on 3 Nov. Revenue +12.5% and accelerating, beta 0.44, net cash, 5.6% off its high rather than at it.
picks.key_risk: Drug-pricing push after a Democratic sweep

picks.thesis: Raised outlook, revenue +10%, RSI 58. Trimmed a point because it sits near its high inside an extreme defensive rotation.
picks.key_risk: Post-midterm drug-pricing shock or rotation unwind

picks.thesis: Record $8.9B revenue (+28%), backlog +46%, raised EPS guide on 3 Nov. Post-earnings drift setup; Bernstein calls data-center fears overblown.
picks.key_risk: Hyperscaler capex cuts; EPS keeps lagging sales

picks.thesis: Intermodal surcharge took effect 2 Nov. Latest quarter +15.3%, 40% operating margin, beta 0.16. No event until January.
picks.key_risk: Freight recession or merger regulatory setback

picks.thesis: Record October volume, Treasury futures +48%. Payrolls, CPI and a contested December FOMC keep rate volatility high. Trimmed because valuation data is unverifiable.
picks.key_risk: Volatility collapses post-election; stock perps take share

picks.thesis: A deliberate starter, not dust. Latest quarter +106% at 26x P/E. Earnings ~17 Nov. Add only if $200 holds after tonight's AMD and ANET read-through.
picks.key_risk: Closes below $200; China cap or capex-digestion guide

picks.thesis: Revenue +26.8% and accelerating, 7.9% FCF yield, 23.5x P/E. December guidance and Trench financing details next; Talen's PJM guide supports power demand.
picks.key_risk: AI-power unwind; Trench leverage concerns

avoid.reason: 6 Nov earnings binary at 41.7x sales, revenue -28%, ~70% above Goldman's $137 target.
10 Nov earnings, 15% bond yield, -47% FCF yield; epicenter of AI-credit stress.
Binary print 4 Nov at 20.6x sales; PLTR and SHOP show beats get sold.
RSI 86 after +27% month; Iran diplomacy or Democratic sweep removes the bid.
Falling knife after weak Q4 guide; -20% net margin, no catalyst until January.

responses.point: MSFT: partly conceded, cut to 7%. But de-grossing sells crowded winners with binaries ahead. MSFT is flat over 12 months, earnings are already out, and growth accelerated to 18.8%. It is the least event-exposed AI holding.

TMUS: conceded that beta -0.47 isn't a structural hedge, and trimmed to 6%. The thesis is an 11.2% FCF yield plus a raised cash outlook already reported. The 28 Oct 8-K details are unknown, so conviction drops to 3.

CME: conceded. The $20.3B cap with no P/E looks like a data error; my general knowledge says the cap is much larger, but that is unverified. Cut to 3% at conviction 2. The volatility catalysts (payrolls, CPI, FOMC) remain dated and real.
JPM: conceded that +27.7% is June data and BAC and SCHW internals are weak. Cut to 6%. I keep it because 13.8x P/E and 16% volatility still beat the XLF basket, and there is no event until January.

IEF and your killer scenario: agreed that hot CPI is the threat, so IEF is capped at 6% and cash rises to 32%. Payrolls (6 Nov) precede CPI, and I will reassess IEF at the next review before CPI lands.
Dust: I hold none under 3%. NVDA 3% is a rule-based starter with an explicit add trigger, not an averaging artifact. Energy is XLE only, so the CVX double-count doesn't apply to me.

APP.summary: AppLovin runs an AI-driven ad platform for mobile apps and is expanding into e-commerce. Revenue growth is +61% with 77% operating margin, but growth is decelerating and the stock is down 67% from its high, with class actions pending.
APP.bull: Exceptional margins, 18.6x P/E and 5.5% FCF yield after a 67% drawdown; a strong print could trigger a sharp rebound.
APP.bear: Growth is decelerating, class actions allege AI disclosure issues, momentum is deeply negative and beta is 2.3. Results could reset the multiple again.
red_flags: Class action lawsuits alleging AI technology disclosure issues

NBIS.summary: Nebius is an AI cloud and infrastructure provider. The stock is down 35% in a month and 49.5% off its high, with 110% volatility. It bounced Tuesday, but no financials were provided and debt market signals look cautious.
NBIS.bull: AI compute demand remains strong, the stock is oversold with RSI 37, and sharp rebounds are possible in this volatile name.
NBIS.bear: Heavy capital needs, debt market caution, high beta of 4 and a broken trend make this a speculative name with no fundamental data provided.
catalysts: Further capital raises or debt financing
AI infrastructure sentiment, led by Oracle and CoreWeave financing news
red_flags: Debt markets signal caution per Seeking Alpha
No revenue or margin data provided

CRWV.summary: CoreWeave is a GPU cloud provider with TTM revenue of $7.6B, growing 115%. It has a negative operating margin, -47% FCF yield and heavy debt, including a 15% bond yield. The stock is down 62% from its high, with earnings due Nov 10.
CRWV.bull: Revenue growth above 100% and a sharp oversold bounce; a good earnings print and easing AI funding fears could drive a squeeze.
CRWV.bear: About $35B of debt, 15% bond yields, deeply negative free cash flow and a heavy capex burn leave little margin for error.
catalysts: Q3 earnings on Nov 10 (implied move about 13%)
AI funding sentiment via Oracle and hyperscalers

NVDA.summary: Nvidia dominates AI accelerators. TTM revenue is $303B, up 83%, with the latest quarter up 106%, 65% operating margin and a 26x P/E. The stock is down 14% from its high after a four-day rout and a China exposure cap.
NVDA.bull: Accelerating growth, huge margins and a 26x P/E for the AI leader; the oversold bounce and valuation support a rebound.
NVDA.bear: China exposure curbs, AI capex digestion fears and debt-funded customer risk; the stock is breaking support near $200.
catalysts: Fiscal Q3 earnings, typically mid-to-late November
China export policy and cloud-client limits
red_flags: Told cloud clients to cap China business at 49%
Four-day selloff and broken technical support
Customer financing strain across AI infrastructure

AVGO.summary: Broadcom makes AI custom silicon, networking and infrastructure software. TTM revenue is $89B, up 49%, with the latest quarter up 85%. The stock is 33% below its high, with rich multiples (17.8x sales) and a new debt filing.
AVGO.bull: Accelerating AI revenue growth, 48% operating margin and a 33% pullback offer a better entry on a durable franchise.
AVGO.bear: Still 17.8x sales, a downtrend below the 50- and 200-day averages, and a new debt raise; AI spending fears could extend weakness.
red_flags: Down 20% over 3 months with a negative trend

AMD.summary: AMD sells CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators. TTM revenue is $41B, up 40%, with the latest quarter up 50%. The stock fell 22% in a month but jumped 5-6% into Q3 earnings, and it trades at 125x P/E and 19x sales.
AMD.bull: Accelerating growth and AI GPU share gains, a Samsung foundry breakthrough and bullish pre-earnings calls; a strong outlook could extend the rebound.
AMD.bear: 125x P/E and 16% operating margin demand a huge outlook; Bloomberg flags AI fears, and beta of 3.3 makes it vulnerable.
catalysts: Q4 guidance and AI GPU roadmap commentary
red_flags: 125x P/E leaves little room for error
Event risk from imminent earnings after a 22% monthly drop

TSM.summary: World's leading foundry and key supplier of leading-edge AI chips. Shares are $405, down 16.6% in a month and 16.9% below the high, in a broad chip rout, yet still up 36% over 12 months and near the 200-day average. RSI 41.
TSM.bull: Leading-edge foundry monopoly with a 2nm ramp underway; AI demand is durable, pullback leaves shares near the 200-day average, and a VP bought stock.
TSM.bear: High beta (2.18) in an ongoing semiconductor rout; Taiwan geopolitical risk; sector momentum is negative and the Iran conflict plus rates near 5% pressure multiples.
catalysts: Monthly Taiwan revenue report in early November
Possible role in Tesla Terafab project

ASML.summary: Sole EUV lithography supplier. Shares $1,561, down 16% in a month and 22% off the high, trading below the 200-day average. Q3 results are out and a buyback is running, but the market is skeptical and the chip sector is weak.
ASML.bull: Monopoly in EUV with a multiyear AI-driven capex cycle, an active buyback, and a pullback that has reset the valuation after a 48% 12-month gain.
ASML.bear: Equipment names are being sold hard, the buyback hasn't stopped the slide, forecast uncertainty remains, and high beta of 2.31 amplifies sector drawdowns.
catalysts: Customer capex updates from TSMC and Micron
red_flags: Buyback failing to halt the slide

MU.summary: Memory maker in an AI-driven supercycle. TTM revenue of $133B is up 256%, with 75% operating margin and a P/E of 11.4x. Shares are $854, down 32% from the high but up 282% in 12 months, and still above the 200-day average.
MU.bull: Extraordinary earnings, a P/E near 11, a 6% FCF yield and a $35B buyback weeks away make the pullback attractive if memory pricing holds.
MU.bear: Memory is cyclical, and 80%+ gross margins imply a peak; any pricing rollover would crush the stock. Beta 3.4, a 39% drawdown, and negative momentum add risk.
catalysts: $35 billion buyback launch expected in coming weeks
red_flags: Peak-cycle margins of 81% gross raise sustainability questions

QCOM.summary: Mobile chip leader pushing into AI and data center. TTM revenue of $44B is up just 1.9%, with the latest quarter down 4%. Shares are $164, 37% below the high, P/E 18.6x, FCF yield 7.2%, ahead of results tomorrow.
QCOM.bull: Cheap at 18.6x earnings with a 7% FCF yield; AI and data center ambitions give optionality, and a CFO who says things can only go up.
QCOM.bear: Revenue is shrinking, handset exposure is weak, memory costs squeeze devices, AI plans are unproven, and the stock lost support heading into earnings.
red_flags: Revenue declining 4% in the latest quarter
Stock broke key support ahead of earnings

INTC.summary: Intel is rebuilding as a chipmaker and foundry. Shares are $61, down 35% in a week and 47.5% in a month after a record October plunge following weak Q4 guidance despite a 78% jump in data center sales. RSI is 22.
INTC.bull: Data center sales jumped 78%, revenue is up 21%, and the foundry has strategic value. The stock is deeply oversold at RSI 22 and could rebound sharply.
INTC.bear: Weak Q4 guidance triggered the worst day since 1974; net margin is -20%, operating margin 3%, and FCF yield 1.2%. Foundry execution remains unproven.
catalysts: Q4 earnings and guidance update in January
red_flags: Net margin -20% with only 3% operating margin
Down 39% vs the 50-day average, falling knife

AMAT.summary: Largest US semiconductor equipment maker. Shares $382, down 29.5% in a month and 48% off the high. TTM revenue is $30.8B, up 7.8%, with the latest quarter up 24.8%. P/E 32.7x with results due November 12.
AMAT.bull: Accelerating growth (+25% latest quarter), 30% operating margin and AI packaging exposure; the sharp derating offers a rebound if earnings and guidance impress.
AMAT.bear: Still 32.7x earnings and a 1.9% FCF yield after a steep drop; equipment stocks are leading the chip rout and momentum is poor below both averages.
catalysts: Besi stake plan and AI packaging update
red_flags: Down 28% over 3 months, trading below the 50- and 200-day averages
Rich P/E relative to recent drawdown and low FCF yield

LRCX.summary: Lam Research makes wafer-fab etch and deposition equipment. Latest quarter revenue grew 54% with a 37% operating margin. The stock is down 33% in a month and 47% off its high, deeply oversold (RSI 28) amid a semiconductor sell-off.
LRCX.bull: Record quarter, accelerating growth and AI-driven fab spending support earnings. A 47% drawdown at 34x earnings gives a better entry point if semis stabilize.
LRCX.bear: Beta of 3.3 and a falling trend: the stock sits 20% below its 50-day average. Semi-equipment cyclicality and supply bottlenecks could cap upside; the sector is still being sold.
catalysts: Semiconductor sector sentiment after the AI sell-off
Next quarterly guidance, expected late January
red_flags: Down 33% in one month with no stabilization yet
Supply bottleneck concerns after record quarter

KLAC.summary: KLA sells process control and inspection tools to chipmakers. Latest quarter revenue grew 29% and net margin is 36%. The stock is down 24.5% in a month and 49% off its high, on a 38.7x P/E.
KLAC.bull: AI and advanced packaging drive inspection demand, and growth is accelerating. Net margin of 36% reflects a dominant franchise now trading far below its peak.
KLAC.bear: High beta, a 14% discount to the 200-day average and a 14x sales multiple leave it exposed if the semiconductor sell-off continues. GF Value suggests it is still overvalued.
catalysts: Semiconductor sentiment and AI capex commentary
Analyst rating changes following the earnings report
Next quarterly report, expected late January
red_flags: Down about 50% from its high, with the downtrend intact

MRVL.summary: Marvell supplies data-center and custom AI silicon. Revenue grew 37% last quarter, but the stock fell 30% in a week after announcing a $115B Lumentum acquisition. Analysts are downgrading, and a combined $91B of value has been lost between the two stocks.
MRVL.bull: Strategic rationale for owning AI optical connectivity is real, RBC sees benefits outweighing risks, and growth is accelerating. The oversold bounce potential is large.
MRVL.bear: The giant deal creates integration risk, dilution and a possible collapse. TD Cowen halved its price target, and the stock trades at 57x earnings with only a 17% operating margin.
catalysts: Shareholder and regulatory reactions to the Lumentum deal
Next earnings, expected late November/early December
red_flags: TD Cowen downgrade and price target halved
Down 30% in a week and 29% below its 50-day average
Rich 57x P/E for a 17% operating margin

ARM.summary: Arm licenses CPU architecture and collects royalties, with 98% gross margin. Revenue grew 22% last quarter. The stock is 55% off its high at 207x earnings, and fiscal Q2 earnings land November 4. It bounced 3.7% today.
ARM.bull: AI demand and rising royalty rates could extend its beat run. A 55% drawdown resets sentiment ahead of earnings, and the royalty model is highly scalable.
ARM.bear: Valuation of 42x sales and 207x earnings is extreme with only a 17% operating margin. Royalty-mix scrutiny and AI demand worries could drive further declines.

TXN.summary: Texas Instruments makes analog and embedded chips. Last quarter revenue grew 28% with a 41% operating margin. The stock is up 99% over 12 months and only 6% below its high, rising while the rest of semis fall.
TXN.bull: The analog recovery is clearly under way, with accelerating growth and high margins. Low beta (1.5) and strong relative strength give it defensive qualities within semis.
TXN.bear: At 40x earnings with a 2.6% FCF yield, expectations are high. RSI of 72 suggests it is stretched, and a $2B notes issue adds debt.
red_flags: Valuation leaves little room for a miss

SNDK.summary: Sandisk makes NAND flash memory. Revenue is up 272% TTM, with a 72% operating margin and a P/E of 8x. The stock is 53% off its high and down 34% in a month, though it rebounded about 7% today.
SNDK.bull: A memory super-cycle is producing extraordinary margins and a 10.9% FCF yield at a single-digit P/E. The price drop leaves the stock cheap if pricing holds.
SNDK.bear: Memory is a peak-cycle business where margins of this size usually mean-revert, so low P/E may be a trap. Beta of 4.1 and an 82% volatility mean violent swings.
catalysts: Next quarterly report, expected late January
red_flags: Peak-cycle margins of 72% may not last

AAPL.summary: Apple beat Q4 with revenue growth of 11.7% on iPhone strength, but the stock fell and broke key support. Rising memory costs threaten margins and analysts flag a services slowdown. Valuation is rich at 36x earnings, with a 2.8% FCF yield.
AAPL.bull: iPhone cycle strength, 33% operating margin, low beta and a huge buyback capacity make it a defensive quality compounder. The 12-month gain of 23% shows leadership.
AAPL.bear: Memory price inflation squeezes gross margin, growth is decelerating, services is slowing, and a 36x P/E leaves little room for a miss. Technicals have turned weak.
catalysts: Holiday-quarter iPhone demand and December-quarter guidance
Memory cost trajectory and margin commentary
red_flags: Broke key technical support after earnings

MSFT.summary: Microsoft posted FY27 Q1 revenue growth of 18.8%, accelerating, with Azure demand exceeding supply. Margins are exceptional (47% operating) and the P/E of 26.9x is moderate for the growth. The stock trades 6% off its high and is flat over 12 months.
MSFT.bull: Accelerating growth at $346B revenue scale, AI demand exceeding capacity, and a large contracted backlog. Valuation is reasonable versus peers while the stock lags its fundamentals.
MSFT.bear: Heavy AI capex weighs on the 1.6% FCF yield, and capacity constraints cap near-term upside. The stock fell 31% at its 12-month drawdown, and the tech sector is in a risk-off phase.
catalysts: Azure capacity additions through the December quarter
FY27 Q2 earnings in late January 2027
red_flags: Low FCF yield of 1.6% on elevated capex
Stock is flat over 12 months despite beats

ORCL.summary: Oracle is a leveraged AI-infrastructure story. Revenue growth is accelerating (29.6% last quarter) but FCF yield is -7.5%, and the stock is down 52% from its high. A $20B stock and bond raise cleared a funding overhang and lifted shares, but dilution and credit risk remain.
ORCL.bull: Accelerating cloud growth and a huge AI backlog, plus 20x P/E, mean a successful buildout could drive a sharp rebound. The funding overhang is now cleared.
ORCL.bear: Negative free cash flow, heavy debt and equity issuance, credit rating pressure, and 59% volatility. The AI build depends on a few large customers and continued financing access.
catalysts: Credit rating agency decisions after the $20B raise
Progress on AI data center capacity and customer contracts
red_flags: $20B equity and debt raise causing dilution

CRM.summary: Salesforce is a cheap, cash-generative software name (19x P/E, 8.3% FCF yield) growing only about 11%, with growth slowing. The stock fell 7.6% this week amid a share offering and a $2.7B Cresta AI acquisition. Trend is mixed, with the stock below its 50-day average.
CRM.bull: Low valuation, strong FCF yield, 77% gross margin and agentic AI products offer re-rating potential if growth stabilizes. Buybacks and acquisitions extend the platform.
CRM.bear: Low-teens growth, deceleration, AI disruption fears for seat-based software, and acquisition spending plus a share offering signal dilution and execution risk.
catalysts: Fiscal Q3 earnings in early December 2026
Cresta integration and Agentforce adoption metrics
Share offering pricing and use of proceeds

ADBE.summary: Adobe is a high-margin (89% gross, 36% operating) software franchise growing 12% at a 13x P/E and 11% FCF yield. The stock is 32% off its high on AI disruption fears. A Redburn target cut weighs on sentiment, while the Premiere Mobile music deals are minor.
ADBE.bull: Extremely cheap on earnings and cash flow, steady growth with strong margins, and AI features like Firefly could prove monetizable. Low beta limits market risk.
ADBE.bear: Generative AI may erode creative-tool moat and pricing power. Growth is flat at about 12%, the stock is down 27% over 12 months, and analysts are cutting targets.
catalysts: Adobe MAX and AI product monetization updates
red_flags: AI disruption narrative driving a de-rating

NOW.summary: ServiceNow plunged about 30% in a week after its Q3 report despite 20.5% revenue growth. Growth is decelerating, operating margin is just 10%, and the P/E is 78x. The stock sits well below both its 50-day average and its high, though analysts like Argus remain bullish.
NOW.bull: 21% growth at scale, a sharp selloff creating a reset valuation, and a 4.2% FCF yield. Analyst targets imply large upside if the AI workflow thesis holds.
NOW.bear: Post-earnings collapse signals broken growth or guidance expectations, 78x GAAP P/E remains high, and momentum is deeply negative. Volatility is 74%.
catalysts: Analyst estimate revisions following the Q3 reset

WDC.summary: Hard-drive maker riding AI data-center storage demand. TTM revenue $14.5B (+43%), latest quarter +55.5%, op margin 39%. Stock $346, down 57% from high and 33% in 3 months, but still +131% over 12 months. P/E 12.9x.
WDC.bull: Accelerating growth, high margins and a low P/E for an AI storage beneficiary; the selloff looks sentiment-driven after a parabolic run.
WDC.bear: Cyclical memory/storage peak fears, with Kioxia's cautious outlook hitting peers. Beta 3.2 and a 57% drawdown show fragile momentum. Net margin of 69% likely includes one-offs.
catalysts: Memory-sector read-throughs from Micron and SanDisk
red_flags: Down 57% from high with trend still broken (17% below 200d)
Net margin 69% well above operating margin suggests non-recurring gains

STX.summary: Hard-drive maker with HAMR ramp tied to AI storage demand. TTM revenue $13.8B (+44%), latest quarter +61%, op margin 40%. Stock $605, down 32% in a month and 47% off the high. Paying down $1.2B of debt.
STX.bull: Revenue acceleration, HAMR product cycle and debt paydown; a 30% monthly drop may overshoot given the earnings trajectory.
STX.bear: Cyclical peak fears and sector de-rating; P/E 31.6x is well above WDC's, leaving less cushion. High beta and a weak trend (23% below 50d).
red_flags: Fell 32% in a month with no technical base yet
Valuation richer than WDC for similar growth

SMCI.summary: AI server maker. TTM revenue $39.1B (+78%), but growth is decelerating sharply (accel -29.5pp), margins are thin (gross 11%, op 7%) and FCF is deeply negative (-33.5% yield). Stock $31.68, down 27% in a month. Earnings are imminent.
SMCI.bull: Cheap at 0.5x sales and 9x earnings, with huge AI server demand and a bounce under way in server peers.
SMCI.bear: Thin margins, heavy cash burn, decelerating growth and a history of governance and auditor problems. Executive changes add to the risk.
catalysts: Fiscal Q1 earnings in early November
red_flags: Past auditor resignation and accounting history (headline)

COHR.summary: Optical and photonics supplier for AI data centers. TTM revenue $7.1B (+22.5%), latest quarter +33.7% and accelerating. Stock $208, down 37.5% in a month and 53% off the high. P/E 51.9x, FCF negative, earnings imminent.
COHR.bull: Growth is accelerating with AI networking demand, and the AI premium has been squeezed out. A Lumentum-related optics tailwind and a bounce are under way.
COHR.bear: Still 52x earnings with negative FCF and 95% volatility. Optical names are in a momentum unwind and earnings could trigger another leg down.
catalysts: Fiscal Q1 earnings in early November
Optical peer results and AI capex commentary
Co-packaged optics deal flow in the sector
red_flags: Earnings binary risk at high volatility

GLW.summary: Materials and glass maker, including optical fiber for AI data centers. TTM revenue $17.7B (+18.8%), op margin 16%. Stock $127.64, down 20% in a month and 53% off the high after Q3 earnings. P/E 51x, FCF yield 3.8%.
GLW.bull: Solid, steady growth with fiber demand from AI buildouts. A selloff attributed to forced selling rather than weak fundamentals could mean reversion.
GLW.bear: Valuation of 51x earnings is rich for 19% growth with no acceleration. De-rating and a broken trend (18% below 200d) may continue.
catalysts: Optical fiber demand updates from hyperscalers
red_flags: P/E 51x with only modest growth acceleration
Down 53% from high with no confirmed bottom

GOOGL.summary: Alphabet: search, YouTube, Cloud and AI. TTM revenue $471B (+22%), latest quarter +24.7%, op margin 33%. Stock $280, down 19% in a month and 31% off the high, RSI 15 (deeply oversold). P/E 14.7x. Raising debt in Europe to fund capex.
GOOGL.bull: Strong growth with huge margins at a 14.7x P/E, deeply oversold, with a diversified AI position across Cloud, search and models.
GOOGL.bear: Heavy AI capex pushes FCF yield to 0.6% and bond issuance; search monetization worries and AI disruption of search weigh on the stock.
catalysts: Search monetization data and analyst revisions
Euro bond sale completion and capex guidance
red_flags: FCF yield only 0.6% as capex surges
Raising debt to fund AI spend
Down 17.5% in October with the trend broken

SNOW.summary: Snowflake is a cloud data platform growing 32% (latest quarter 35%, accelerating) but still deeply unprofitable (op margin -23%). Stock is down 13% in a week and 23% off its high, yet up 109% over 6 months at 19x sales.
SNOW.bull: Growth is accelerating on AI data demand and Jefferies names it a better AI bet than Palantir. The pullback gives a cheaper entry into a strong 6-month uptrend.
SNOW.bear: 19x sales with -23% operating margin and 1.1% FCF yield leaves little cushion. Software and AI names are selling off, and a Seeking Alpha downgrade flags a catch in the AI flywheel.
catalysts: Datadog Q3 results on Nov 4 as a read-through for data and observability software
Next quarterly earnings, expected late November/early December
Progress on AI agent and gateway product rollouts
red_flags: Falling 12% in a week with RSI 35 and a 56% one-year max drawdown

DDOG.summary: Datadog is a cloud observability platform growing 31.5% (latest quarter 35.6%, accelerating) with 80% gross margin but roughly breakeven operations. Stock has fallen 22% in a week ahead of Q3 results on Wednesday, at 20.6x sales.
DDOG.bull: Growth is accelerating on AI observability demand and Wedbush expects another beat-and-raise. The 22% drop sets a lower bar into earnings.
DDOG.bear: Valuation of 20.6x sales and 460x earnings is rich, and UBS flags valuation risk. The sector is selling off, so even a beat may not hold.
catalysts: Guidance for Q4 and 2027 and AI-native customer growth
Software sector sentiment after Palantir results
red_flags: Fell about 22% in one week with 76% volatility
Operating margin around 0% and P/E of 460x
Binary earnings event within a day

SHOP.summary: Shopify is an e-commerce platform growing 32.5% with a 15% operating margin. It fell as much as 16% after Q3 revenue and GMV ($119B) missed and holiday-quarter guidance disappointed. RSI is 26, and it trades at 13.5x sales and about 90x earnings.
SHOP.bull: Growth is still above 30% and operating income jumped 66%. The oversold, guidance-driven selloff may prove an overreaction for a profitable scaled leader.
SHOP.bear: Missed revenue and GMV with weak holiday guidance and decelerating growth, at a premium valuation. Beta of 1.8 magnifies downside if sentiment stays weak.
catalysts: Analyst estimate revisions in the days after earnings

DELL.summary: Dell sells servers, PCs and AI infrastructure, with revenue up 49% (latest quarter 58%) at thin 20% gross margin. Stock is down 26% over a month and 31% off its high but bounced about 4-5% today. At 1.8x sales and 23x earnings.
DELL.bull: Booming AI server demand, cheap multiples versus peers, and a heavily oversold chart. Sector bounce suggests dip buyers are active.
DELL.bear: Growth is decelerating sharply and margins are thin. Beta of 2.5 means AI-trade unwinds hit hard, and the stock is still far below recent highs with a broken trend.
catalysts: Super Micro earnings as read-through for AI servers
Dell fiscal Q3 earnings in late November
AI server order and backlog updates

ANET.summary: Arista makes high-speed data center networking gear, with revenue up 32.6% (latest quarter 37.7%) and 43% operating margin. Stock is down 18% in a month, below its 50-day, and reports Q3 results after the close today at 20x sales.
ANET.bull: Eight straight beats, accelerating growth and elite margins on AI networking buildout. A 22% drawdown resets expectations ahead of earnings.
ANET.bear: Margin guidance risk and a 20x sales multiple. Stock has broken its 200-day line and the AI hardware trade is under pressure.
catalysts: Q3 earnings after the close on Nov 3
Q4 and 2027 guidance on gross margin and AI revenue targets
red_flags: Earnings today after the close, binary outcome

CSCO.summary: Cisco is a networking and security giant, with revenue up 11.8% (latest quarter 17.6%), 24% operating margin and $9.3B in AI orders. Stock fell 9% after earnings despite a beat and is 21% off its high at 30.7x earnings.
CSCO.bull: Growth is accelerating on AI infrastructure orders with strong cash generation and a 3.1% FCF yield. Low volatility and the pullback improve entry.
CSCO.bear: A beat still sold off 9%, signaling stretched expectations. 30x earnings is rich for a mature hardware firm, and the trend has weakened with 3-month -14.7%.
catalysts: AI order updates and hyperscaler wins

INTU.summary: Intuit (TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, Mailchimp) trades $348, down 47% over 12 months but up 23% in the last month. Revenue growth is 13.9% and accelerating, with a 21% net margin, 20x P/E and 9.3% FCF yield. RSI is 67 after the bounce.
INTU.bull: Cheap versus history at 20x earnings with a 9% FCF yield, accelerating growth, and a steady AI rollout. The first-half reset leaves room for a rebound.
INTU.bear: AI disruption fears keep pressuring software multiples. The stock is still below its 200-day average and has bounced sharply, so a 1m +23% gain could fade.
catalysts: Tax-season guidance and AI product updates ahead of the TurboTax cycle
red_flags: Software sector softness cut shares 3% in one session

PLTR.summary: Palantir sells data and AI platforms to governments and companies. Q3 revenue passed $2B, up about 96% year over year, with a 46% operating margin. The stock fell about 12% on the week after the report on slowing total contract value, and RSI is 30.
PLTR.bull: Exceptional growth with high margins, commercial demand now exceeding government, and sovereign AI tailwinds. The oversold pullback could attract buyers.
PLTR.bear: At 62x sales and 123x earnings, any deceleration is punished. Outlook signals slower AI-fueled growth and weaker bookings.
catalysts: Post-earnings analyst revisions and bookings commentary over coming weeks
red_flags: Total contract value slowdown flagged by analysts
Valuation of 62x sales leaves no margin for error
Beta near 2 and a 49% drawdown in the past year

IBM.summary: IBM is a hybrid cloud, AI consulting and software company, with mainframes as a cash engine. Revenue is $69.9B, up 6.8%, with a 16% net margin, 21x P/E and 6.2% FCF yield. The stock is up 13% in a month and RSI is 72, so it looks short-term extended.
IBM.bull: Reasonable valuation, strong free cash flow, a defensive profile with beta 0.82, and AI product launches. The stock could recover more of its 25% decline from its high.
IBM.bear: Growth is mid-single digit, the stock is overbought after a sharp run, and it is only barely above its 200-day average. Software disruption fears remain.
catalysts: AI product rollouts and client adoption updates
red_flags: Overbought at RSI 72 after a 13% monthly gain

CRWD.summary: CrowdStrike is a cloud endpoint and security platform. It announced two AI security acquisitions (including Fiddler) and an AI agent kill switch. The stock has doubled in 6 months, though it is down 8% on the week. Valuation metrics are unavailable and FCF yield is 0.6%.
CRWD.bull: Leading position in AI agent security, an expanding platform, and a Claude Cowork integration. Momentum remains strong, 46% above its 200-day average.
CRWD.bear: A $252B market cap on a 0.6% FCF yield prices in perfection. Beta 1.55 and 72% volatility mean sharp drawdowns in a risk-off tape.
catalysts: Integration of the two announced AI security acquisitions
Q3 FY27 earnings in early December 2026
red_flags: Rich valuation with FCF yield of 0.6%
Down 8% in 1 week and 10% in 1 month as software and tech weaken

PANW.summary: Palo Alto Networks is a network, cloud and security platform vendor. Revenue is $11.5B, up 24.5%, with the latest quarter up 34.5%, aided by acquisitions. Operating margin is 6% and net margin 3%. The stock is up 93% in 6 months but down 12% in a week.
PANW.bull: Platform consolidation in security, accelerating growth and AI-driven demand. Pullback from the high may offer a better entry.
PANW.bear: At 25x sales and 947x earnings, valuation is stretched, margins are thin, and acquisition-fueled growth may flatter organic trends.
catalysts: Fiscal Q1 earnings in mid-to-late November 2026
red_flags: Down 12% on the week amid a falling tech sector

NET.summary: Cloudflare provides edge network, security and developer services. Revenue is $2.5B, up 33.5%, with an operating margin of -14%. The stock is down 23% in a month and 16% in a week, with RSI at 35, ahead of Nov 5 earnings. JPMorgan upgraded it to overweight.
NET.bull: Growth is accelerating above 30%, AI traffic and edge demand are tailwinds, and the pullback with a JPMorgan upgrade sets up a reset before earnings.
NET.bear: At 39x sales with negative operating margins and FCF yield of 0.4%, any guidance miss could extend the selloff. Momentum is sharply negative.

MELI.summary: Latin American e-commerce and fintech leader. Revenue grew 41% TTM with accelerating growth, 12% operating margin, 16% FCF yield. Stock is down 29% from its high, oversold (RSI 30), and reports Q3 on Nov 4.
MELI.bull: Accelerating 40%+ growth, fintech and logistics scale, oversold shares at 3.5x sales and a high FCF yield give a strong earnings-reaction setup.
MELI.bear: Operating margin of 12% is thin for a 45x P/E. Heavy investment in credit and shipping could squeeze profit again. Earnings risk is binary after a weak trend.
catalysts: Credit book quality and margin commentary
red_flags: Downtrend: -28% over 12 months, below 50d and 200d averages
Binary earnings event the day after the brief

EBAY.summary: Online marketplace with 72% gross margin, 20% operating margin and 16% TTM growth. Stock is up 50% in 12 months, near its high after Q3 results. Valuation is 25x earnings with a 4.6% FCF yield. Insider selling is small.
EBAY.bull: Broad-based growth, AI-driven marketplace improvements, strong cash generation, and low beta make for steady compounding with analyst support.
EBAY.bear: After a 50% run, valuation is full, growth is decelerating, and spending on strategic investments could pressure margins.
red_flags: Executive Form 4 sale of 2,366 shares at $121.86 (minor)
Restructuring costs noted in the Oct 22 8-K

PG.summary: Largest US household-products company. Revenue grew 3.5% TTM with a 4% latest quarter, 23% operating margin, and a 23x P/E. Shares are up 12% in a month, near highs after fiscal Q1 results.
PG.bull: Defensive earnings, accelerating organic growth, pricing power, and a reliable dividend make it a good haven in a volatile, rate-sensitive market.
PG.bear: Low growth at 23x earnings leaves limited upside after a 12% monthly rally. Input costs and consumer trade-down are risks.
catalysts: Fiscal Q2 earnings in late January
red_flags: Executive selling at $165, including a CEO-level sale of 38,253 shares for $6.3M
A note offering due 2076 signals long-dated financing

KO.summary: Global beverage concentrate leader. Revenue grew 7% TTM with 30% operating margin and fresh Q3 beats with raised guidance. Stock is up 41% in 12 months and 1.4% below its high at 28x earnings.
KO.bull: Volume-led growth, global pricing power, exceptional margins, and an upgraded 2026 outlook make it a premier defensive compounder.
KO.bear: The 28x P/E and 3.5% FCF yield leave little margin for error, with softer North American demand a watch item.
catalysts: Bottler results such as CCEP and KOF
red_flags: Reports of softer North American demand
Stretched valuation after a 22% six-month rally

PEP.summary: Beverage and snack giant (Frito-Lay, Pepsi). Shares are 19% below their high and have rebounded 10% in a month, but remain under the 200d average. Valuation and financial data are missing from the feed, so the view is limited.
PEP.bull: Laggard versus KO with a rebound underway, a diversified snack portfolio, and a dividend income appeal make for a catch-up trade.
PEP.bear: Underperformance versus Coca-Cola reflects weak snack volumes and consumer pressure. The stock is below its 200d average and fundamentals are unverified here.
red_flags: No revenue, margin or valuation data supplied
Max drawdown of 25% over the past year

DKNG.summary: Online sports betting and iGaming operator. Revenue was up 15% TTM but fell 4.6% in the latest quarter, with a slight operating loss. Shares are 41% below their high but have bounced to an overbought RSI of 74.
DKNG.bull: Possible 2027 profit inflection, a 6% FCF yield, a 1.7x P/S multiple, and analyst targets of $27-$30 imply large upside if sentiment recovers.
DKNG.bear: Revenue contraction, prediction-market competition, regulatory pushback (Utah halt), and a Bernstein target cut weigh on an extremely volatile stock.
red_flags: Latest-quarter revenue down 4.6%, a 21-point growth deceleration
RSI 74 after a sharp bounce; 51% volatility

MCD.summary: Global burger franchisor with 46% operating margin and steady cash flow. Shares bounced 12.5% in a month into Q3 earnings but remain 23% off the high. RSI 78 shows it is overbought. Revenue growth is slowing (latest quarter +3.7%).
MCD.bull: Defensive franchise model, high margins, 21x P/E and 4.2% FCF yield. Value-menu and US traffic recovery could extend the rebound in a volatile market.
MCD.bear: Quarterly growth is decelerating and the stock is overbought after a sharp run into earnings. Low-income consumer weakness and a McRib class action add pressure.
catalysts: US comparable sales and traffic trend
red_flags: McRib marketing class action allowed to proceed

NKE.summary: Global athletic brand in a turnaround. Revenue is shrinking (TTM -1.2%, latest quarter -4.3%) and the stock is down 39% over 12 months and 44% off its high, but it has rebounded 13% in a month. Valuation is low at 10.6x P/E with a 6.4% FCF yield.
NKE.bull: Depressed valuation, 43% gross margin and a 6.4% FCF yield leave room for a sharp rerating if the turnaround and inventory cleanup show up in sales.
NKE.bear: Sales are still falling, restructuring costs continue and competitors have taken share. The stock is 16% below its 200-day average, so the rebound may fade.
catalysts: Holiday wholesale and direct sales trends
red_flags: Max drawdown of 49% over the past year

SBUX.summary: Global coffee chain in a turnaround with a China transition. Shares are up 32% over 12 months and near highs, RSI 81. At 60x P/E and 8% operating margin, the valuation prices in a lot of recovery. Latest quarterly revenue fell 1.4%.
SBUX.bull: US momentum, margin recovery and a long-term international store expansion plan. Analyst coverage is positive, with price target raises and new initiations.
SBUX.bear: Valuation is stretched at 60x earnings, international growth is slow, revenue dipped in the latest quarter and the stock is extremely overbought.

BKNG.summary: Dominant online travel platform with a 33% operating margin and an 8.4% FCF yield. Shares are down 26.5% over 3 months and 31% off the high on slowing room-night growth and AI-agent disintermediation fears. Q3 results are imminent.
BKNG.bull: Cheap versus history on cash flow, strong margins and buybacks. A solid Q3 and reassurance on AI agents could trigger a sharp relief rally.
BKNG.bear: Room-night growth is slowing and revenue growth is decelerating. AI agents could cut direct traffic, and UBS issued a pessimistic target.
red_flags: Revenue growth slowed 8pp in the latest quarter

UBER.summary: Global mobility and delivery platform growing revenue 16.7% TTM with 12% operating margin and 7.4% FCF yield. Shares are down 31% over 12 months and 33% off the high on robotaxi worries. Earnings are due Wednesday.
UBER.bull: Cheap at 14x P/E with strong free cash flow, double-digit growth and an expanding footprint. A good Q3 print could close the gap to analyst targets.
UBER.bear: Autonomous vehicles may disintermediate the platform, robotaxi spending is ramping, and options imply a sharp earnings move. The Delivery Hero bid adds deal risk.
red_flags: Rising AV investment pressures cash flow

ABNB.summary: Global short-term rental marketplace with 21% operating margin and revenue growth of 13.6% TTM, latest quarter +16.5%. Shares are up 33% over 12 months and above the 200-day average. At 37x P/E, much is priced in ahead of Q3 results.
ABNB.bull: Strong growth, high margins and an Amex partnership. Analysts are raising targets, and trend and momentum are positive.
ABNB.bear: Premium valuation at 37x earnings and 7.6x sales leaves little room for a miss. Travel demand is sensitive to weak consumer sentiment and growth is decelerating.

TTWO.summary: Take-Two publishes GTA, NBA 2K and mobile titles. Revenue TTM $6.7B (+15%) but latest quarter only +2%, with a slight operating loss. Shares are down 24% over 12 months and 11% below the 200-day average, with GTA VI sentiment driving the stock.
TTWO.bull: GTA VI launch could be a record seller (Piper sees 45M launch-period units), and Wedbush argues its earnings power is more durable than the market expects.
TTWO.bear: Wedbush cut its target on lower earnings forecasts. Growth has slowed, margins are negative and FCF yield is under 1%. A GTA delay or soft launch would hit the stock.
catalysts: GTA VI launch timing and marketing updates
Fiscal Q2 earnings, expected in early November (date not given)
red_flags: Valuation relies on one title's launch

AMZN.summary: Amazon spans retail, AWS and ads. TTM revenue $797.5B (+15%), operating margin 13%, P/E 19.9x, FCF yield 6.3%. Q3 results came on Oct 29. Shares are 13.5% off their high and near the 200-day average.
AMZN.bull: AWS growth and a price-target hike signal AI demand. Valuation is reasonable at about 20x earnings with a 6% FCF yield, after a 9% three-month pullback.
AMZN.bear: Quarterly growth slowed to +12% (down 7.5pp). AI capex reportedly exceeds operating cash flow, and the high beta of 1.43 adds risk in a tech sell-off.
catalysts: AWS growth and capex commentary in coming weeks
red_flags: Heavy AI capex versus operating cash flow

TSLA.summary: Tesla makes EVs, energy storage and autonomy software. TTM revenue $103.6B (+8%) but latest quarter -0.2%. Operating margin 3%, P/E 479x, P/S 15x. Shares are up 24% in three months and trade near $400 amid SpaceX merger speculation.
TSLA.bull: Autonomy and robotics optionality plus a possible SpaceX tie-up keep sentiment strong. Momentum is positive and China sales are up 21% year to date.
TSLA.bear: Valuation of 479x earnings is extreme given flat quarterly revenue and a thin 3% operating margin. Merger uncertainty and Musk governance add risk, with beta 2.15.
catalysts: Monthly China and Europe delivery data
red_flags: Revenue fell in the latest quarter
Governance risk from SpaceX merger talks

COST.summary: Costco is a membership warehouse retailer. Shares are $1,022, up 11% in a month and 6.8% below their high, with RSI 63. Financial metrics were not provided here. The 10-K was filed Oct 7, and the stock-split chatter is speculation.
COST.bull: Membership model delivers steady comps and renewal strength. The defensive profile suits a volatile tape, and a possible 2027 split could add retail demand.
COST.bear: The stock is extended after an 11% monthly gain. It has historically traded at a premium multiple, leaving little room for error. No valuation data is provided here.
catalysts: Fiscal Q1 earnings in late November or December (date not given)

WMT.summary: Walmart is the largest US retailer, with grocery, e-commerce and advertising. TTM revenue $728.5B (+6%), operating margin 4%, P/E 44.9x, FCF yield 1.4%. Shares rose 19% in a month, RSI 70, and trade about 8% below their high.
WMT.bull: Steady share gains, growing ad and membership income, and defensive appeal. A $6B robotics partnership aims at automation-driven margin gains.
WMT.bear: At about 45x earnings with a 1.4% FCF yield, the stock is priced for perfection. It is overbought after a 19% monthly run, with growth steady rather than accelerating.
catalysts: Q3 FY27 earnings in mid-November (date not given)

HD.summary: Home Depot is the leading home-improvement retailer. TTM revenue $169.2B (+2.5%), latest quarter +5.7%, operating margin 12%, P/E 23.2x, FCF yield 5.7%. Shares jumped 18% in a month but are still down 10% over 12 months.
HD.bull: Reasonable valuation and a high FCF yield, with growth improving. Falling long yields would help housing-linked demand, and one target implies 17.5% upside.
HD.bear: Housing turnover remains weak with 10-year yields near 4.9%. The stock is overbought after an 18% monthly run (RSI 73) and sits at the top of its range.
catalysts: Q3 earnings on Nov 17, 9 a.m. ET

MA.summary: Global card network with 59% operating margin. Q3 revenue grew 14% and the company held its 2026 outlook. Stock is up 15% in a month, 2% off its high, RSI 70, at a premium valuation. Low beta and agentic-commerce partnerships support it.
MA.bull: Durable double-digit growth, very high margins, low beta, and AI/agentic commerce partnerships (OpenAI, Tencent) extend the cross-border and value-added services runway.
MA.bear: Sharp run-up leaves RSI at 70 and the stock stretched. Consumer sentiment is weak, and regulatory and interchange litigation risk persists.
catalysts: Holiday spending and cross-border travel data in November-December
Agentic commerce rollout updates with OpenAI
Credit Card Competition Act and interchange settlement news

AXP.summary: Premium card issuer and network. TTM revenue is $43.9B, up 8.9%, with Q3 growth slowing to 7.8%. P/E is 17.8x. The stock is 16% below its high but flat versus its 200-day average, and rebounding after Q3 results.
AXP.bull: Affluent customer base, fee-driven model and a reasonable 17.8x P/E. Analyst targets are being raised and the stock is rebounding from a deep drawdown.
AXP.bear: Revenue growth is decelerating and the stock is down 8.8% over 12 months. Credit losses could rise with weak sentiment, and rewards costs are heavy. Officers are selling shares.
catalysts: Credit quality and delinquency monthly updates
Fed rate path and consumer data
red_flags: Officer proposed share sales via option exercises

BRK-B.summary: Diversified conglomerate with insurance, railroad, utilities and a large equity portfolio, now led by Greg Abel. Shares sit at the 52-week high with very low volatility. RSI is 76 and Q3 earnings are imminent.
BRK-B.bull: Fortress balance sheet, huge cash pile, defensive profile and a rare 14% volatility. Abel's new picks are helping, and the shares have historically risen in most years.
BRK-B.bear: Overbought at RSI 76 right at the highs. A new leader's stock-picking record is questioned, with a loss on Alphabet cited. Growth is modest.
catalysts: Q3 earnings release in early November
Capital deployment of the cash pile under Abel
Insurance underwriting results and catastrophe losses
red_flags: Barron's critique of the stock-picking record

BX.summary: Largest alternative asset manager. Q2 revenue grew 36% and TTM growth is 17%, with a P/E of 25x. The stock is 28% below its high and is bouncing, with heavy AI and energy infrastructure deal activity. Volatility is high.
BX.bull: Deep discount to its high, accelerating revenue, and AI and energy infrastructure deployment (VoltaGrid, LNG Canada). Fundraising and realizations could rebound with lower rates.
BX.bear: Private-credit and real-estate worries and higher long yields weigh on valuation. Beta is 1.32 and a 37% drawdown shows the risk. Credit spreads are widening.
catalysts: Realization and fundraising updates in Q4

ICE.summary: Exchange, clearing and data operator that owns the NYSE and mortgage-tech businesses. Q3 revenue grew 21% and the stock is up 10% in a week, 3% from its high. P/E is 23x. It faces pushback on the OKX tokenized-stock plan.
ICE.bull: Accelerating revenue, recurring data and clearing income, and volatility-driven volumes. The tokenization partnership offers an option on new markets.
ICE.bear: Stretched after a 66% multi-year run and a 10% weekly gain, with RSI 69. Over 50 issuers are objecting to the OKX tokenized-stock plan, and volumes may fade.
catalysts: SEC response deadline on OKX-ICE tokenized stock plan
Energy and rates trading volumes amid Iran tensions
red_flags: Broad issuer objections to the tokenized-stock plan
Extended after a sharp weekly rally

CME.summary: Dominant derivatives exchange across rates, equity index, energy and metals. It posted record October volume, with Treasury contract volume up 48%. Q3 revenue grew 13% at a 66% operating margin. The stock is up 13% in a month, 7% off its high.
CME.bull: Volatility, rate uncertainty and the Iran war lift volumes. Record market data revenue and a high operating margin add to the case.
CME.bear: Earnings depend on volatility, which can fade. The stock has already rallied 16% in 3 months. Insider selling is notable and crypto/perp competition is growing.
catalysts: Monthly volume report in early December
red_flags: Senior managing director sold $3.08M of stock
Earnings tied to volatility that may normalize

BABA.summary: Chinese e-commerce and cloud giant trading at $100, down 44.7% from its high and 40.7% over 12 months. It is deeply oversold (RSI 23, 20% below its 200-day). No financials were provided, and the news flow is thin.
BABA.bull: Extreme oversold reading and a deep drawdown could set up a sharp rebound. Cloud and AI work, including Qwen in Apple Intelligence in China, offers a re-rating angle.
BABA.bear: Persistent downtrend with no support yet. China consumer and regulatory risk remain, and no earnings or valuation data were provided to anchor a floor.
catalysts: China stimulus or consumer data prints
Qwen and Apple Intelligence rollout progress
red_flags: Down 22% in 3 months and below both moving averages
Fundamentals not supplied, so valuation cannot be checked
Qwen/Apple headline accompanied a stock slip

JPM.summary: Largest US bank by market cap ($894B). TTM revenue is $199.4B, up 13.5%, with a 33% net margin. The P/E is 13.8x. The stock is 8% off its high, above its 200-day, with low volatility (beta 0.75).
JPM.bull: Best-in-class franchise with strong revenue acceleration, a reasonable valuation, and defensive beta. It should benefit from a capital markets rebound after the midterms.
JPM.bear: Credit spreads are widening, consumer sentiment is weak, and the 3-month return is -5.9%. A midterm-driven market drop could hit trading and sentiment.
catalysts: Q3 earnings already out; watch Q4 results in mid-January
Fed path and yield curve moves
red_flags: Scrutiny over external AI agent curbs, which is minor

BAC.summary: Large US bank, $341.8B cap, P/E 10.6x. TTM revenue is $120.2B, up 5.4%, but the latest quarter grew only 3.2% and growth is decelerating. The stock is down 21% in 3 months and 24% off its high, with RSI at 32.
BAC.bull: Cheap at 10.6x earnings and sharply oversold. A rebound in markets could bring mean reversion, and its scale and deposit base are strong.
BAC.bear: Growth is slowing, momentum is poor (11% below its 50-day), and a settlement charge and AML order add regulatory overhang.
catalysts: Fed rate path and yield curve
red_flags: Down 21% in 3 months, well below its peers

GS.summary: Top investment bank with a $257.6B cap and P/E of 11.6x. TTM revenue is $69.7B, up 18.7%, with a 32% net margin. The stock is 22.6% off its high after a 3-month slide of 15%. CEO flags strong AI deal demand.
GS.bull: Cheap for its growth, with a deal pipeline supported by AI-related M&A and a likely post-midterm capital markets reopening. A fresh 10-Q is filed.
GS.bear: High beta (1.68) means it falls hard in a correction. Revenue growth is decelerating, and trading and deal revenue is cyclical.
red_flags: Beta of 1.68 and a 24% max drawdown

MS.summary: Wealth and investment banking leader with a $291B cap and P/E of 14.4x. TTM revenue is $78.0B, up 18%, with accelerating growth and a 26% net margin. The stock is 20% off its high with a 3-month return of -14.5%.
MS.bull: Growth is accelerating, wealth management gives stable fees, and its own strategists call the correction in its final stage. It should gain from a post-midterm rally.
MS.bear: At a P/E of 14.4x it is pricier than GS, beta is 1.46, and a market correction would weigh on fee and trading revenue.
red_flags: 3-month slide of 14.5% with the stock below its 50-day
Higher valuation than the other banks

V.summary: Global payments network with a $197.8B cap and P/S of 8.6x. TTM revenue is $23.0B, up 11.5%, with the latest quarter up 12.9%. The stock is near its high (1.2% below) after a 14% monthly rally. RSI is 73 and insiders are selling.
V.bull: Steady double-digit growth, a low beta of 0.27, strong momentum after earnings, and expansion in China through the Tencent MoU. A defensive winner in a volatile market.
V.bear: Overbought after a 14% month and stalling below resistance near $426.7. A premium valuation leaves little room for error, and insiders are selling.
catalysts: Pullback toward the 50-day for a better entry
red_flags: Insider selling by a director and an officer
Net margin and P/E data are stale or missing

ISRG.summary: Maker of da Vinci surgical robots with a recurring instrument and service base. Revenue growth is accelerating (+21.7% latest quarter) with 28% operating margin. The stock is up 16.5% over 3 months but 27.6% below its high, at 51x earnings.
ISRG.bull: Procedure growth is accelerating, recurring revenue gives visibility, margins are high, and the stock is rebounding with room to recover its prior high.
ISRG.bear: A 51x P/E leaves little room for error. A reported $450M antitrust charge and insider selling add overhang. Competition is rising.
catalysts: Antitrust charge details and any further litigation developments
Aaron Martin joins the board Jan 1, 2027
red_flags: Insider selling by a VP and a controller

TMO.summary: Life-science tools and diagnostics leader with $47.4B TTM revenue, +9.1% latest quarter growth and 18% operating margin. Q3 beat and raised 2026 guidance. The stock is up 49.7% in 6 months and sits 2% below its high at 36.5x earnings.
TMO.bull: Guidance raise, resilient demand and a low beta of 0.62 support steady compounding. Biopharma tools spending looks to be recovering.
TMO.bear: After a 50% run in six months, valuation looks full at 36.5x. Growth decelerated slightly, and there is little cushion if tools demand softens.
catalysts: Q4 earnings and 2027 guidance in late January 2027
red_flags: Stretched after a 26% premium to its 200-day average

VRTX.summary: Cystic fibrosis franchise leader with 38% operating margin and $12.6B TTM revenue. Q3 revenue beat, EPS lagged, and 2026 sales guidance was raised. Several analysts lifted price targets to $563-$640. The stock trades 5.6% below its high at 31x earnings.
VRTX.bull: Guidance raise, accelerating growth, a net-cash franchise and a pipeline (pain, kidney, diabetes) offer upside with low beta of 0.44.
VRTX.bear: Heavy dependence on cystic fibrosis. The Q3 EPS miss and pipeline execution risk could limit gains, with consensus targets implying only ~5% upside.
catalysts: Pipeline data readouts in pain, kidney and diabetes programs
Q4 earnings and 2027 guidance in early 2027

AMGN.summary: Large-cap biotech with $38.1B TTM revenue, +9.5% latest quarter growth and 30% operating margin. The stock is up 59.7% over 12 months and 14.4% in 3 months, with RSI 74 (overbought) ahead of the Q3 report, at 28.7x earnings and a 4.1% FCF yield.
AMGN.bull: Accelerating growth, solid FCF yield, low beta and a strong rerating could extend if Q3 results and pipeline updates impress.
AMGN.bear: Overbought after a 15% monthly surge into earnings. Expectations are high, mature products face erosion and a miss could prompt a sharp pullback.

HIMS.summary: Telehealth platform for weight loss, sexual health and dermatology with $2.6B TTM revenue and 38% latest quarter growth, but operating margin is -6%. The stock is down 47% from its high, 43.7% over 12 months, with Q3 earnings caution and a class action.
HIMS.bull: Rapid subscriber and revenue growth, a 68% gross margin and a depressed valuation at 2.3x sales give high rebound potential if profitability improves.
HIMS.bear: Operating losses, regulatory and compounded GLP-1 risk, securities litigation and extreme volatility (70% vol, beta 2.8) make the downside severe.
catalysts: Securities class action lead plaintiff deadlines
FDA and GLP-1 compounding policy developments

MRNA.summary: mRNA vaccine and oncology developer with revenue down 27.6% TTM to $2.2B and a -149% operating margin. The stock has risen 314% in 3 months and 757% in 12 months to a $93B cap (41.7x sales) ahead of Nov 6 earnings.

redteam.statement: The consensus isn't reckless, but it is muddled. Six positions under 1.5% (TMO, ISRG, INTU, PG, JNJ, NVDA) come from averaging seven seats. The 'negative betas' on TMUS, CME and XLE are one-year regime artifacts, not structural hedges. XLE already holds CVX, so the 6.8% energy sleeve is less diversified than it looks. The real crash hedge is cash. IEF loses if October CPI is hot. Consolidate the dust, merge the energy sleeve, and admit that MSFT at 8.4% is the book's single largest AI de-grossing bet.

attacks.argument: Twenty-five names, six under 1.5%. TMO 0.6, ISRG 0.8, INTU 0.8, PG 0.9, JNJ 1.0 and NVDA 1.5 are committee averaging artifacts. They pay round-trip costs, dilute attention and cannot move returns. Size each to a real conviction weight or remove it.

Roughly 23% sits in defensives near their highs: KO 1.4% off, BRK-B 0.3% off at RSI 76, ABBV and TMO about 2-3% off. That rotation is the most extreme since 2009. A post-midterm tech relief rally or a strong NVDA print unwinds it together.

The largest weight at 8.4%, held by 8 seats, because it is the only mega-cap with an intact trend. JPM names AI de-grossing as the key risk, and de-grossing sells what still has gains. Beta 1.01, max drawdown -31%, FCF yield 1.6%, and ETFs were net sellers Friday.

Treated as an uncrowded defensive, but it is down 24% over 12 months and 16% below its 200-day, with an executive-change 8-K on 28 Oct and SpaceX satellite competition. As a leveraged carrier it behaves like a bond proxy if the 10-year breaks 5%. The beta of -0.47 is not a structural hedge.
XLE is heavily weighted to XOM and CVX (general knowledge, not in the book). XLE 4.0% plus CVX 2.8% is double exposure to one name. An Iran deal hits both together. Consolidate into XLE.

The book shows a $20.3B cap with no P/E, which is likely broken data. The thesis needs volatility to persist after the election and payrolls. Stock perpetual futures were cleared today, which adds competition. 2.5% rests on unverified valuation.

The '+27.7% revenue' figure is from June data. Meanwhile BAC is -21% over 3 months, SCHW -17% for unexplained reasons, HY spreads +65bp, and private-credit worries are rising. The sector's internals are weaker than the XLF headline suggests.

0.8%, one seat, 51x P/E with a $450M antitrust overhang; either size it or drop it.

Overlaps XLE's top holdings; fold the weight into XLE for clean energy exposure.

blind_spots: Negative betas on TMUS, CME, XLE, KO and PG were measured during a defensive and energy rally; in a liquidity de-grossing, correlations converge.
A Democratic sweep is priced at ~66%, which brings drug-pricing headlines onto ~10.5% health care (ABBV, VRTX, JNJ, ISRG, TMO) that the council treats as safe.
The pending order fills at the open after tonight's AMD, ANET and possibly SMCI prints. Gap risk hits NVDA, ETN, GEV and TXN before any review.
Data gaps (CME cap, stale JPM/V/NEE financials) mean some weights rest on numbers no one has verified.
redteam.killer_scenario: October CPI runs hot around 10-13 Nov after an unremarkable payrolls print. A December hike gets locked in, the 10-year breaks 5.2% and IEF falls. Bond-proxy defensives (KO, PG, TMUS, JNJ) de-rate, AI de-grossing hits MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN, and widening credit drags JPM. Only the 6.8% energy sleeve offsets.

risk.statement: The consensus is defensible, but it gets filled after the election results and tonight's AMD and ANET prints, so I'm tightening rather than loosening. I veto three names on credit, governance or binary grounds: CRWV, SMCI and MRNA. MSFT is capped at 8% because it is the book's largest de-grossing bet. NVDA is capped at 4% into its estimated 17 Nov print, with an exit on a close below $200. TMUS, CME and BRK-B get caps for an unexplained 8-K, broken data and a print at RSI 76. Cash stays at 25% or more, and SHY does not count as cash. No sector above 25%. Keep energy to one sleeve and stay at 15 names or fewer, so no averaging dust.

vetoes.reason: 15% bond yield, -47% FCF yield, about $35B debt, earnings 10 Nov. This is AI-credit stress, not an equity bet.
11% gross margin, -33.5% FCF yield, a history of auditor and governance problems, and multiple executive-change 8-Ks in October.
$93B cap on revenue down 28%, 366% volatility, about 70% above Goldman's target, binary earnings 6 Nov.

concerns: Combined AI-capex exposure (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, ETN, GEV, TXN) should stay at or below 25%. JPM names AI de-grossing as the key election-week risk, and these names fall together.

Killer scenario: hot October CPI (about 10-13 Nov) locks in a December hike and the 10-year breaks 5.2%. IEF, the bond-proxy defensives and credit-sensitive JPM fall together. Cash and SHY are the hedge, not duration.
Energy must be one sleeve of at most 10%. Holding XLE alongside CVX doubles exposure to the same Iran-deal downside, and WTI has already fallen two days on diplomacy hopes.

About 23% of the book sits in low-beta defensives bought at the most extreme equal-weight rotation since 2009. A post-midterm or NVDA-led tech rally unwinds them all at once, so trim the names near their highs (BRK-B, KO).

Hold 15 names or fewer and nothing under 2%. Sub-1.5% averaging artifacts (TMO, ISRG, JNJ, EBAY, META) pay round-trip costs without moving returns. Hard exit rules: MSFT on a close below its 50-day (about $514), NVDA on a close below $200.

chairRaw.statement: We go from all cash to 73% invested, with 27% in cash. That clears the risk manager's 25% floor, and SHY does not count toward it. The book has 15 names and nothing under 3%. The AI-capex factor (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, ETN, GEV) totals 24%, inside the 25% cap. MSFT is 6% because it sits only 0.6% above its 50-day, and it exits on a close below about $514. NVDA is a 3% starter that exits below $200. Energy is one XLE sleeve at 8%, with CVX folded in. I cut IEF, because hot CPI is our killer scenario and cash hedges a crash without duration risk. I also cut BRK-B and KO, defensives sitting at their highs. Defensives must earn their place on raised guidance or cash yield: ABBV, VRTX, UNP, TMUS, ADBE. This order fills after the election and the AMD and ANET results, so the exit rules are binding, not advisory.

responses.point: Conceded on CVX. XLE's largest holdings overlap it (general knowledge, not in the book). I fold CVX into XLE at 10%, keeping one inflation and Iran hedge rather than paying for the same exposure twice.
Conceded on IEF. Your hot-CPI path hurts it, so I cut it from 6% to 4%. SHY, with a -1% max drawdown, goes to 12% and cash rises to 26%. I agree cash is the real crash hedge.
Partly conceded on TMUS. The -0.47 beta is a one-year artifact, so I trim to 7%. The holding rests on an 11.2% FCF yield at 14.7x P/E and the raised cash outlook, not on hedge properties.
Conceded on CME. A $20.3B cap with no P/E is likely broken data, so I trim to 3%. The thesis rests on the reported record volume and 66% margin, with CPI and the December FOMC as near-term catalysts.

Fair on JPM's June-dated revenue and on BAC and SCHW weakness, so I trim to 5%. On MSFT: yes, it's my AI bet, and I size it at 6%, not 8.4%. On dust: my smallest position is 3%. BRK-B and KO are trimmed for being near their highs.

harbor.statement: Vex lands four hits and I'm changing the book. First, I'm folding CVX into XLE at 10% total. That cuts the double count on CVX and leaves less energy than the 11% I had. Second, TMUS's -0.47 beta is a one-year artifact. I cut it to 5% and hold it as an 11% FCF-yield value name, not a hedge. Third, I'm dropping JNJ and PG; at 3% each they were near-dust in crowded staples. Fourth, IEF goes to 3%, because a hot CPI print hurts it. The freed weight goes to cash, which Vex rightly calls the clean crash hedge. I keep SHY, energy, ABBV and VRTX on raised guidance. The cost is 4-6 points of lag if the midterms and NVDA rip.

# Oazy Council briefing: Tue 3 Nov 2026, about 18:00 GMT

I only got one round of searches before the tool limit cut me off. Anything marked **[UNCONFIRMED]** comes from a single source, an estimate, or my own inference.

## 1. Market-moving news, last 7 days

**Midterm elections (today, 3 Nov)**
- Midday trade was mixed. 
The S&P 500 edged up 0.28%, the Dow slipped 0.49%, the Nasdaq gained 0.81% and the Russell 2000 lost 0.21%.

- JPM's base case is a Democratic House and Senate, which it puts at 
66% odds, with the S&P 500 between down 0.25% and up 0.50%.

- JPM says 
the feared AI sell-off on regulation is likely limited
. Its main risk is de-grossing within the AI theme.
- Results will land overnight and tomorrow. The reaction function for AI, software and defense names is the thing to watch.

**Apple (AAPL) and Palantir (PLTR) fell despite beats (reported 2 Nov after the close)**
- 
Apple fell after a disappointing margin forecast and weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter iPad sales.
 The stock was about -2.4% to -2.6% midday.
- 
Palantir beat Q3 expectations and raised full-year guidance. Investors focused on a sharp slowdown in new contract bookings and valuation worries.
 The stock was down about 1.5% to 4.9% depending on the time of the quote.
- The read-across is that beats are not enough for richly valued AI and software names. Bookings and margins are what matter. This is relevant for NOW, CRM, SNOW, DDOG and APP.

**Rates and the Fed**
- Fed funds sit at 3.75–4.00%. 
As of 2 Nov, OIS pricing implied a 73% chance of a 25bp hike at the 9 Dec meeting
, with about 54bp of net hikes priced over 12 months.
- That is a hawkish tilt driven by inflation. I did not confirm what happened at the 27–28 Oct FOMC meeting or who dissented **[UNCONFIRMED]**.
- Kiplinger says the FOMC is focused on inflation and sees no instability in the labor market.
- Implication: this is a headwind for long-duration assets (TLT, IGV, unprofitable growth). Banks and financials (XLF) are less exposed.

**Energy and geopolitics**
- 
Brent rose about 1% to $105.78 and WTI to $97.50.
 Middle East tensions are the driver.
- One analyst said 
a diplomatic breakthrough in the Middle East could lower energy prices and inflation expectations.

- Energy is tied to the rate-hike story: XLE, XOM, CVX, COP, OXY and USO benefit while oil stays high, and it is a headwind for airlines and consumers. I could not confirm the specific event behind the move **[UNCONFIRMED]**.

**China**
- 
The tech-heavy Star 50 fell 3.8% today, erasing Monday's rally. The CSI 300 closed 0.2% lower.

- Beijing has reloaded its 2024-style stock support tools, but the market was unconvinced. This is a negative signal for FXI, BABA and possibly EWT/EWY via sentiment.

## 2. Calendar, next two weeks

**Earnings, this week**
- **Tue 3 Nov, after the close:** AMD, AMGN, ANET (per Market Chameleon). Supermicro (SMCI) also reports Tue per Blofin **[UNCONFIRMED timing]**.
- **Tue 3 Nov, before the open:** SHOP, ETN, BKNG, PFE (per Market Chameleon). Their results may already be out, and I did not check them.
- **Wed 4 Nov:** MCD and QCOM (per Moomoo). Arm and Uber also appear in a preview list this week, but I did not confirm their dates **[UNCONFIRMED]**.
- **Fri 6 Nov:** Moderna (MRNA).
- Other universe names (DDOG, CRWV, NBIS, DKNG, HOOD, COIN and others) are likely to report this week or next. I did not verify them **[UNCONFIRMED]**.

**Earnings, next week**
- **NVDA is estimated for 17 Nov after the close.** 
TipRanks says this is not confirmed.
 Consensus EPS is about $2.47.
- Retail reports are expected the week of 9 Nov and 16 Nov (WMT, HD, COST, and possibly CSCO and AMAT). I did not verify these dates **[UNCONFIRMED]**.

**Macro**
- **Fri 6 Nov, 8:30 ET: October payrolls.**
  - Forecasts are mostly low: Barclays 50k, KPMG 45k, Continuum 50k. One outlier expects 65k.
  - 
September's gain was 29k and unemployment was 4.2%.
 July and August were revised down by a combined 60k.
  - A weak print against a Fed priced for hikes would be a stagflation signal.
- **Two ISM surveys** are due this week, probably the manufacturing and services readings **[UNCONFIRMED dates]**.
- **CPI** for October is likely around 10–13 Nov. I did not confirm the date or consensus **[UNCONFIRMED]**.
- **Wed 18 Nov, 14:00 ET: minutes of the late-October FOMC meeting.** Look here for the hawkish detail.
- **Next FOMC: 8–9 Dec**, with a dot plot.
- Not checked: index rebalances, options expiry on 20 Nov, Treasury refunding, and the Japan and ECB schedules **[UNCONFIRMED]**.

## 3. Sentiment, positioning and flows

- **Sentiment on AI is fragile.** Commentary describes doubts about AI monetization and capex. One Seeking Alpha piece refers to an "unfolding AI bubble burst", which is an opinion and not a data point. Good results from Apple and Palantir were sold, which shows a lack of buying appetite for high-valuation tech.
- **De-grossing risk.** JPM names de-grossing within AI as the key election-related risk. I found no hard data on hedge fund exposure, ETF flows (SMH, QQQ, IBIT) or retail activity **[UNCONFIRMED]**.
- **Divergence.** The Nasdaq 100 is leading while the Dow and Russell 2000 lag. Mega-cap tech is still the support, which raises the stakes on NVDA and AMD.
- **Rate pressure.** Hike pricing, mortgage rates and gasoline are all rising. Continuum flags a risk of lost economic momentum in Q4.

## Suggested council focus

1. **Election outcome and the AI regulation read.** Tomorrow's tape will show whether JPM's "buy the dip" view holds.
2. **AMD and ANET results tonight.** These set the tone for semiconductors and AI networking, including NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, COHR and SMCI.
3. **Friday's payrolls against 73% hike odds.**
4. **Oil near $100.** It is a risk for inflation and for the rate path.

**Not covered because of the search limit:** the Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon earnings reaction from late October, the October FOMC decision details, CPI timing, crypto and gold levels, and Treasury yields.

That combination punishes duration-heavy growth, and the tape agrees: semis are down 24% over the month while health care and energy lead. I want low risk: 25% cash earning about 4%, a short-duration bond sleeve, energy as the inflation and geopolitical hedge, and cash-rich, low-beta compounders. If the midterms, payrolls and NVDA pass cleanly, add quality growth rather than chase beta.
